entries.not_relevant_because: The problem asks for the exact values of W(r,k) (and the off-diagonal numbers w(r; k_1,...,k_r)) across all r and k. The family's manuscript, Quantitative Superexponential Bounds for van der Waerden Numbers, proves only growth bounds: W_r(k) > k^(ck*floor(log_2 r)) for k at least an absolute K_0 and all r >= 2 (c = 10^-5), and W_r(k) > exp((log r)^2/(64 log 2)) for r >= 256 and k >= 3. It also gives a recursive finite upper bound. None of these fixes a value of any nontrivial W(r,k), and the only exact values it states (W_1(k) = k, W_r(1) = 1, W_r(2) = r+1) are the trivial cases the problem does not ask for; the manuscript does not treat off-diagonal numbers.
